# Foundations of Training {#sec-theory-training}

Part I asked you to run a training job. This chapter asks why training
works at all, and why the dials you set in @sec-eng-training have the
effect they do. We move from the loop to the optimization and statistics
beneath it.

By the end you will be able to explain why a schedule, batch size, or
parallelism choice changes the result, not just that it does.

## Learning as optimization

The loss surface, gradients, and what a step of stochastic gradient
descent does to the parameters in expectation.

## Stochastic gradient methods

Variance of the gradient estimate, momentum, adaptive methods, and the
bias and variance each trades.

## Scaling laws

How loss falls with parameters, data, and compute, what the exponents
mean, and how to use them to plan a run.

$$
L(N, D) = L_\infty + \left(\frac{N_c}{N}\right)^{\alpha_N} + \left(\frac{D_c}{D}\right)^{\alpha_D}
$$

## Batch size and learning rate

The relationship between batch size, gradient noise, and the largest
useful step, and why the two must move together.

## Generalization

Why an overparameterized model can still generalize, the role of implicit
regularization, and what the training loss does and does not tell you.

## Distributed optimization

What data and model parallelism do to the optimization problem, the cost
of synchronization, and the effect of stale or compressed gradients.
